title: Teacher-student relationship and teaching styles in primary education. A model of analysis.
venue: Journal of Professional Capital and Community
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether students’ perceptions of their teachers’ teaching styles are associated with their perceptions of the teacher-student relationship in primary education. The authors focus on two teaching-style dimensions—directive and participative—and two relationship dimensions—emotional and educational—arguing that these constructs are often studied separately but should be analyzed together.

Using survey data from the 2018/2019 Diagnostic Assessment in the Canary Islands, the study applies structural equation modeling to 21,126 sixth-grade students in 623 schools. The latent variables are constructed from existing questionnaire items rather than from direct observation. The paper also compares perceptions across student subgroups defined by gender, relative age, and parents’ educational level.

The findings indicate that participative teaching style is more strongly associated with both emotional and educational teacher-student relationships than directive style. The directive style relates more to the educational relationship than the emotional one, while participative style is more strongly linked to the emotional relationship. The study also finds that perceptions differ by gender and parental education, with girls generally perceiving more participative teaching and more positive relationships, and students from less-educated families perceiving directive teaching more clearly. The paper concludes that student feedback can be used to model classroom relationships, but it is limited by the use of pre-existing questionnaire data and the absence of some dimensions such as discipline/conflict management.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring system is an adaptive educational system that provides instruction, practice, and feedback based on learner responses.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper does not study an AI tool; it cites prior literature on teaching styles and teacher-student relationships, including references to student feedback questionnaires and related educational constructs.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a correlational, non-AI paper analyzing relationships between teaching styles and teacher-student perceptions using survey data and SEM. It does not evaluate an AI tool, so there is no tool-level evidence quality to rate beyond the paper being non-experimental for AI.
impact_tier_rationale: No AI intervention or AI-assisted coaching tool is studied, so there is no direct impact on instructional coaching or lesson-plan feedback to assess.
